name: PDF placement
description: Where a PDF page lands on the media, and how sharply it is drawn. The page is document.pdf, a 4 by 6 inch label, printed at its own size so it has room to move on a larger sheet: a page fitted to the sheet has nowhere to go, and every anchor would look the same. None of these is a print option in the protocol sense: each is geometry applied while the page becomes pixels, so every job names PDFium: a placement applies only when the job chooses an engine, which then renders it even where the printer or the queue reads PDF itself, and a channel that renders nothing fails the job and says so. The references name it too, so every sheet comes from the same engine. Print the set on the stock you actually use and measure it with a ruler: the first two jobs are the references, the next four move the label, and the last three change what is drawn rather than where. Every other job is drawn as vectors and the rest rendered as bitmaps, starting with vectors, so the placement is measured on both Windows spooler paths: the two must agree to the millimetre. Over IPP or CUPS every page is a raster, so the vector jobs print bitmaps there and report Rendering as dropped.

jobs.description: drawn as vectors: page 1 of pages.pdf fitted to the sheet: the fitted reference, which fills the stock and so cannot show a placement
rendered as a bitmap: the label at its own size, centred: the reference sheet to measure the others against
drawn as vectors: the label against the top left corner of the stock, which is how a label is registered
rendered as a bitmap: top left, then 15 mm right and 10 mm down: the correction a printer that lays its stock off its own origin needs, large enough to measure
drawn as vectors: bottom right with the same offset, to show the anchor is the corner and not a direction: the offset now moves the label off the stock, and what fits is printed
rendered as a bitmap: the label centred along the top edge, the anchor that is neither a corner nor the centre
drawn as vectors: smoothing off: the barcode edges arrive hard rather than as a grey ramp the printer has to halftone. Compare the bars with the centred reference

rendered as a bitmap: the media taken from the document: the label is its own 4 by 6 inch media, so nothing is fitted, moved or resampled. A printer loaded with larger stock reports a size mismatch, which is the printer telling the truth

drawn as vectors: a media size the printer has no name for: 100 by 150 mm, which is close to but not the 4 by 6 inch label. The page carries no size name. A printer loaded with other stock reports a size mismatch
